questions.question: Which equation represents the standard enthalpy change of formation of ethanol, C2H5OH(l)? A 2C(g) + 6H(g) + O(g) -> C2H5OH(l), B 2C(s) + 3H2(g) + 1/2O2(g) -> C2H5OH(l), C 2C(s) + 6H(g) + 1/2O2(g) -> C2H5OH(l), D C2H4(g) + H2O(l) -> C2H5OH(l).
steps: Enthalpy change of formation is the enthalpy change when 1 mol of a compound forms from its elements in their standard states.
Carbon is solid (graphite), hydrogen and oxygen are diatomic gases, so the reactants are 2C(s), 3H2(g) and 1/2O2(g): option B.
A and C start from gaseous atoms, which are not the standard states of the elements; D forms ethanol from two compounds, not from elements.

questions.question: 25.0 cm^3 of 2.00 mol dm^-3 hydrochloric acid is mixed with 25.0 cm^3 of 2.00 mol dm^-3 sodium hydroxide solution in an insulated cup. The temperature rises by 13.7 K. Assume that the mixture has density 1.00 g cm^-3 and specific heat capacity 4.18 J g^-1 K^-1. What is the enthalpy change of neutralisation? A -28.6 kJ mol^-1, B -2.86 kJ mol^-1, C -57.3 kJ mol^-1, D +57.3 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Mass of solution = 50.0 g, so q = m c Delta T = 50.0 x 4.18 x 13.7 = 2863 J = 2.86 kJ.
Moles of HCl (and of NaOH) = 0.0250 x 2.00 = 0.0500 mol, so Delta H = -2.86 / 0.0500 = -57.3 kJ mol^-1 (negative because the temperature rises).
A uses a mass of 25.0 g instead of 50.0 g; B forgets to divide by the moles; D has the wrong sign for an exothermic reaction.

questions.question: Define the term standard enthalpy change of combustion.
questions.answer: The enthalpy change when 1 mol of a substance is completely burned in oxygen under standard conditions, with all reactants and products in their standard states
steps: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burned completely in (excess) oxygen
Under standard conditions (a pressure of 100 kPa and a stated temperature, usually 298 K), with all reactants and products in their standard states
accept: Reacts fully / completely with oxygen, in place of "burned completely"
Standard pressure given as 1 bar (100 kPa)
Complete combustion to the oxides, for example CO2(g) and H2O(l) for an organic compound
Temperature of 298 K (25 C) stated

questions.question: Calculate the standard enthalpy change of formation of propanone, CH3COCH3(l), using the standard enthalpy changes of combustion: C(s) = -394 kJ mol^-1, H2(g) = -286 kJ mol^-1, CH3COCH3(l) = -1790 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Formation equation: 3C(s) + 3H2(g) + 1/2O2(g) -> CH3COCH3(l).
Hess cycle: the elements and propanone both burn to give 3CO2(g) + 3H2O(l), so Delta fH = sum of Delta cH(reactants) - Delta cH(propanone).
Delta fH(propanone) = -250 kJ mol^-1

questions.question: Ammonia is oxidised to nitrogen monoxide in the first stage of nitric acid manufacture: 4NH3(g) + 5O2(g) -> 4NO(g) + 6H2O(g). Calculate the standard enthalpy change for this reaction, using the standard enthalpy changes of formation: NH3(g) = -46.1 kJ mol^-1, NO(g) = +90.3 kJ mol^-1, H2O(g) = -241.8 kJ mol^-1.
questions.answer: -905 kJ mol^-1 (for the equation as written)
steps: Delta rH = sum of Delta fH(products) - sum of Delta fH(reactants).
Reactants: 4(-46.1) + 5(0) = -184.4 kJ mol^-1, because Delta fH of the element O2(g) is zero.

questions.question: A student burned propan-1-ol, C3H7OH, in a spirit burner to heat 150 g of water in a copper calorimeter. The temperature of the water rose from 19.5 C to 46.9 C. Calculate the energy transferred to the water, in kJ. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g^-1 K^-1.
steps: Temperature rise = 46.9 - 19.5 = 27.4 K.

questions.question: In an experiment, 0.583 g of propan-1-ol, C3H7OH (M = 60.0 g mol^-1), was burned and the energy transferred to the water was 17.2 kJ. Calculate the experimental enthalpy change of combustion of propan-1-ol, giving your answer to 3 significant figures with a sign and units.
steps: Moles of propan-1-ol = 0.583 / 60.0 = 0.00972 mol.
Energy released per mole = 17.2 / 0.00972 = 1770 kJ mol^-1.
Combustion is exothermic, so Delta cH = -1770 kJ mol^-1.

questions.question: The Data Booklet value for the standard enthalpy change of combustion of propan-1-ol is -2021 kJ mol^-1. Suggest two reasons why the student's value of -1770 kJ mol^-1 is less exothermic.
questions.answer: Any two: heat lost to the surroundings; incomplete combustion; evaporation of propan-1-ol; heat absorbed by the calorimeter
steps: Heat is lost to the surroundings, so not all the energy released is transferred to the water
Incomplete combustion of the propan-1-ol (soot or carbon monoxide formed), so less energy is released per mole
accept: Some energy heats the copper calorimeter (or the thermometer) rather than the water
Some propan-1-ol evaporates from the burner without burning
Conditions are not standard (for example the water formed is not liquid at 298 K, or the temperature is not 298 K)

questions.question: Each reading on the thermometer used to measure the water temperature has an uncertainty of +/- 0.5 K. The temperature rise measured was 27.4 K. Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the temperature rise.
steps: Two readings are used to find the temperature rise, so the uncertainty in the rise is 2 x 0.5 = +/- 1.0 K.
Percentage uncertainty = 1.0 / 27.4 x 100 = 3.6%.

questions.question: Calculate the standard enthalpy change for the hydrogenation of cyclohexene, C6H10(l) + H2(g) -> C6H12(l), using the standard enthalpy changes of combustion: cyclohexene = -3752 kJ mol^-1, cyclohexane = -3920 kJ mol^-1, hydrogen = -286 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Hess cycle: cyclohexene + hydrogen and cyclohexane all burn to give 6CO2(g) + 6H2O(l).
Delta H = Delta cH(C6H10) + Delta cH(H2) - Delta cH(C6H12) = (-3752) + (-286) - (-3920).
Delta H = -118 kJ mol^-1

questions.question: The enthalpy change of hydrogenation of cyclohexene, C6H10 + H2 -> C6H12, is -118 kJ mol^-1. The measured enthalpy change for the hydrogenation of benzene, C6H6(l) + 3H2(g) -> C6H12(l), is -205 kJ mol^-1. Calculate the value expected for benzene if it contained three separate C=C bonds like the one in cyclohexene, and the difference between this and the measured value.
questions.answer: Expected -354 kJ mol^-1; the measured value is 149 kJ mol^-1 less exothermic
steps: Three C=C bonds would each be hydrogenated with -118 kJ mol^-1: 3 x (-118) = -354 kJ mol^-1 (1 mark).
Measured value is -205 kJ mol^-1 (1 mark).
Difference = -205 - (-354) = +149 kJ mol^-1: benzene releases 149 kJ mol^-1 less energy than expected (1 mark).

questions.question: The measured enthalpy change of hydrogenation of benzene is 149 kJ mol^-1 less exothermic than the value expected for three separate C=C bonds. Deduce what this shows about the structure of benzene.
questions.answer: Benzene is more stable than a ring of three localised C=C bonds, because its pi electrons are delocalised
steps: Benzene is more stable (lower in energy) than the hypothetical molecule with three localised C=C bonds, because it releases less energy when hydrogenated
Benzene has delocalised pi electrons round the ring, so it does not contain three separate C=C double bonds
accept: The delocalisation stabilises benzene by about 149 kJ mol^-1
All the carbon-carbon bonds in benzene are the same length, between the length of a single bond and a double bond
The Kekule structure with alternating single and double bonds is not a correct model of benzene

questions.question: The enthalpy change for the reaction CH4(g) -> C(g) + 4H(g) is +1664 kJ mol^-1. What is the mean bond enthalpy of the C-H bond in methane? A +555 kJ mol^-1, B +416 kJ mol^-1, C +1664 kJ mol^-1, D +6656 kJ mol^-1.
steps: The reaction breaks four C-H bonds, so the mean bond enthalpy = 1664 / 4 = +416 kJ mol^-1.
A divides by 3 instead of 4; C is the energy for all four bonds; D multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.

questions.question: Use the mean bond enthalpies C=C 612, C-C 347, C-H 413 and H-H 436 (all in kJ mol^-1) to find the enthalpy change for C2H4(g) + H2(g) -> C2H6(g). A +125 kJ mol^-1, B +288 kJ mol^-1, C -125 kJ mol^-1, D -1173 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Bonds broken: C=C + H-H = 612 + 436 = 1048 kJ mol^-1.
Bonds made: C-C + 2 C-H = 347 + 826 = 1173 kJ mol^-1.
Delta H = 1048 - 1173 = -125 kJ mol^-1. A has the wrong sign, B counts only one C-H bond made, D is the energy of the bonds made only.

questions.question: Define the term mean bond enthalpy.
questions.answer: The enthalpy change to break 1 mol of a covalent bond in gaseous molecules, averaged over a range of different compounds
steps: The enthalpy change when one mole of a covalent bond is broken, with the molecules in the gaseous state (gaseous molecules to gaseous atoms)
The value is an average taken over a variety of compounds containing that bond
accept: Energy required to break one mole of bonds in the gaseous state, averaged over different molecules
Mean (average) of the bond dissociation enthalpies of that bond in different environments
The enthalpy change for X-Y(g) -> X(g) + Y(g), averaged over a range of compounds

questions.question: Show that the mean bond enthalpy of the O-H bond is about +463 kJ mol^-1, using the enthalpy change of formation of water vapour, H2(g) + 1/2O2(g) -> H2O(g), Delta H = -241.8 kJ mol^-1, and the bond enthalpies H-H = +436 kJ mol^-1 and O=O = +498 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Bonds broken: 1 H-H and 1/2 O=O = 436 + 249 = 685 kJ mol^-1.
Bonds made: 2 O-H bonds = 2E(O-H).
Delta H = bonds broken - bonds made, so -241.8 = 685 - 2E(O-H).

questions.question: Use the mean bond enthalpies C-C 347, C-H 413, O=O 498, C=O (in CO2) 805 and O-H 464 (all in kJ mol^-1) to calculate the enthalpy change for the combustion of propane: C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) -> 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(g).
steps: Bonds broken: 2 C-C + 8 C-H + 5 O=O = 694 + 3304 + 2490 = 6488 kJ mol^-1.
Bonds made: 6 C=O + 8 O-H = 4830 + 3712 = 8542 kJ mol^-1.

questions.question: The standard enthalpy change of combustion of propane, measured experimentally with liquid water as a product, is -2220 kJ mol^-1. The bond enthalpy calculation for 4 mol of water vapour gives -2054 kJ mol^-1. Suggest two reasons why the values differ.
questions.answer: Mean bond enthalpies are averages; the experimental value is for liquid water (condensation releases energy)
steps: Mean bond enthalpies are averages over many compounds, so they are not exact for the bonds in propane, CO2 and H2O
The experimental value is for liquid water but the calculation uses gaseous water; condensing 4 mol of water releases extra energy
accept: Bond enthalpies refer to gaseous species, whereas the experimental value refers to standard states (liquid water at 298 K)
The C-C, C-H and O-H bond enthalpies are averages that differ slightly from the actual values in propane and water

questions.question: Using your answer to (a), -2054 kJ mol^-1 for C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) -> 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(g), and the enthalpy change of vaporisation of water, +44.0 kJ mol^-1, calculate Delta H for C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) -> 3CO2(g) + 4H2O(l). Compare this with the experimental value of -2220 kJ mol^-1.
questions.answer: -2230 kJ mol^-1; it agrees with -2220 kJ mol^-1 to within 0.5%
steps: Condensing 4 mol of water releases 4 x 44.0 = 176 kJ.
This is within 10 kJ mol^-1 (about 0.5%) of -2220, so the remaining difference is small and is due to using mean bond enthalpies.

questions.question: Ethanol vapour can be dehydrated to ethene: C2H5OH(g) -> C2H4(g) + H2O(g). Use the mean bond enthalpies C-C 347, C=C 612, C-H 413, C-O 358 and O-H 464 (all in kJ mol^-1) to calculate the enthalpy change for this reaction.
steps: Bonds broken in ethanol: C-C + 5 C-H + C-O + O-H = 347 + 2065 + 358 + 464 = 3234 kJ mol^-1.
Bonds made: C=C + 4 C-H in ethene, and 2 O-H in water = 612 + 1652 + 928 = 3192 kJ mol^-1.

questions.question: Explain why a bond enthalpy calculation would give a less reliable value of Delta H for the dehydration of liquid ethanol than for gaseous ethanol.
questions.answer: Mean bond enthalpies apply to gaseous molecules; for a liquid, energy is also needed to overcome intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds), which the calculation ignores
steps: Mean bond enthalpies are defined for bonds in gaseous molecules
Liquid ethanol has hydrogen bonds and other intermolecular forces; the extra energy to separate the molecules (vaporise the liquid) is not included in the bond enthalpy calculation
accept: The enthalpy change of vaporisation of ethanol would have to be added to the calculated value
The bond enthalpy of O-H in liquid ethanol differs from the mean value because of hydrogen bonding
The product water would be liquid, not gaseous, so its condensation also has to be allowed for

questions.question: The mean bond enthalpies of C-Cl, C-Br and C-I are +346, +290 and +228 kJ mol^-1. Explain, in terms of bond enthalpy, why 1-iodobutane is hydrolysed by aqueous sodium hydroxide faster than 1-chlorobutane under the same conditions.
questions.answer: The C-I bond is the weakest, so it needs the least energy to break, giving the lowest activation energy and the fastest reaction
steps: The C-I bond has the lowest bond enthalpy (+228 kJ mol^-1) so it is the weakest of the three bonds
Less energy is needed to break the C-I bond, so the activation energy of the hydrolysis is lower
A greater proportion of collisions has at least the activation energy, so the rate is faster
accept: C-I bond is longer and the bonding electrons are further from the nucleus, so the bond is weaker
The rate-determining step involves breaking the carbon-halogen bond
The C-Cl bond (+346 kJ mol^-1) is the strongest, so chlorobutane is hydrolysed most slowly

questions.question: Which equation represents the lattice energy of magnesium oxide? A Mg2+(g) + O2-(g) -> MgO(s); B Mg(s) + 1/2O2(g) -> MgO(s); C Mg2+(aq) + O2-(aq) -> MgO(s); D MgO(s) -> Mg2+(g) + O2-(g).
steps: Lattice energy is defined as the enthalpy change when 1 mol of an ionic solid forms from its gaseous ions, so it is exothermic.
B is the enthalpy change of formation, C uses aqueous ions, and D is the reverse process (lattice dissociation enthalpy).

questions.question: Which compound is predicted to have the most exothermic lattice energy? A LiF, B NaCl, C CaS, D MgO.
steps: Lattice energy becomes more exothermic as the ionic charges increase and as the ionic radii decrease.
MgO and CaS both contain 2+ and 2- ions, so they are more exothermic than LiF and NaCl.
Mg2+ and O2- are smaller than Ca2+ and S2-, so the ions in MgO are closer together and attract more strongly: D.

questions.question: Calculate the enthalpy change of solution of magnesium chloride, MgCl2(s) -> Mg2+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq), using the lattice energy of MgCl2 = -2526 kJ mol^-1 and the enthalpy changes of hydration: Mg2+(g) = -1920 kJ mol^-1, Cl-(g) = -364 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Energy cycle: MgCl2(s) -> Mg2+(g) + 2Cl-(g) is the reverse of the lattice energy, so +2526 kJ mol^-1.
Then hydrate the gaseous ions: -1920 + 2(-364) = -2648 kJ mol^-1.

questions.question: Explain why the lattice energy of magnesium oxide, MgO, is more exothermic than the lattice energy of calcium oxide, CaO.
questions.answer: Mg2+ is smaller than Ca2+, so it has a higher charge density and attracts O2- more strongly
steps: Both oxides contain ions with the same charges, 2+ and 2-, so the difference comes from the ionic radii
Mg2+ is smaller than Ca2+ (one fewer electron shell), so the ions are closer together and the charge density of the cation is higher
The electrostatic attraction between the ions in MgO is stronger, so more energy is released when the lattice forms
accept: Distance between the nuclei of the ions is smaller in MgO
Lattice energy depends on the charges on the ions and the sum of the ionic radii
MgO has the more exothermic lattice energy because the ionic bonding is stronger

questions.question: Write an equation, with state symbols, to represent the second electron affinity of oxygen.
steps: The second electron affinity is the enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous O- ions gains one mole of electrons to form gaseous O2- ions.
Equation: O-(g) + e- -> O2-(g), with the electron shown on the left and state symbols on every species.

questions.question: Use the following data to calculate the lattice energy of calcium oxide, CaO. Enthalpy change of formation of CaO = -635 kJ mol^-1; enthalpy change of atomisation of calcium = +178 kJ mol^-1; first ionisation energy of calcium = +590 kJ mol^-1; second ionisation energy of calcium = +1145 kJ mol^-1; enthalpy change of atomisation of oxygen, 1/2O2(g) -> O(g) = +249 kJ mol^-1; first electron affinity of oxygen = -141 kJ mol^-1; second electron affinity of oxygen = +798 kJ mol^-1.
steps: Hess's law: Delta fH = Delta atH(Ca) + IE1 + IE2 + Delta atH(O) + EA1 + EA2 + lattice energy (1 mark for a correct cycle or expression).
Sum of the terms other than the lattice energy = 178 + 590 + 1145 + 249 + (-141) + 798 (1 mark for all six terms with correct signs).
This sum = +2819 kJ mol^-1 (1 mark).
Lattice energy = -635 - 2819 = -3454 kJ mol^-1 (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain why the second electron affinity of oxygen is endothermic, whereas the first electron affinity of oxygen is exothermic.
questions.answer: The O- ion is negatively charged and repels the incoming electron, so energy must be supplied
steps: The first electron is added to a neutral atom and is attracted by the nucleus, so energy is released (exothermic)
The second electron is added to a negative ion, O-, which repels it; energy must be supplied to force the electron on (endothermic)
accept: Repulsion between the negative ion and the incoming electron outweighs the attraction to the nucleus
The energy released when the O2- lattice forms (the lattice energy) compensates for the endothermic second electron affinity
Second electron affinity is positive because the electron is added to an ion with a negative charge

questions.question: The lattice energy of CaO calculated from the ionic model is -3401 kJ mol^-1. Compare this with the value from the Born-Haber cycle, -3454 kJ mol^-1, and state what the comparison suggests about the bonding in calcium oxide.
questions.answer: The two values are similar (within about 2%), so CaO is almost completely ionic with very little covalent character
steps: The Born-Haber value (-3454 kJ mol^-1) is only slightly more exothermic than the ionic-model value (-3401 kJ mol^-1), a difference of about 1.6%
The ionic model, which assumes perfectly spherical ions with purely electrostatic attraction, fits well, so calcium oxide is almost purely ionic
accept: The small difference suggests a small degree of covalent character because Ca2+ slightly polarises the O2- ion
The experimental (Born-Haber) value being more exothermic than the ionic-model value means the ionic model slightly underestimates the attraction
A large difference would show significant covalent character

questions.question: Calculate the enthalpy change of formation of the hypothetical compound MgCl(s) from the following data (all in kJ mol^-1): atomisation of magnesium = +148; first ionisation energy of magnesium = +738; atomisation of 1/2Cl2(g) = +122; electron affinity of chlorine = -349; lattice energy of MgCl = -753.
steps: Delta fH(MgCl) = Delta atH(Mg) + IE1 + Delta atH(Cl) + EA(Cl) + lattice energy.
= -94 kJ mol^-1

questions.question: Calculate the enthalpy change of formation of MgCl2(s) from the following data (all in kJ mol^-1): atomisation of magnesium = +148; first ionisation energy of magnesium = +738; second ionisation energy of magnesium = +1451; atomisation of 1/2Cl2(g) = +122; electron affinity of chlorine = -349; lattice energy of MgCl2 = -2526.
steps: Two chlorine atoms are needed, so the atomisation and electron affinity terms are doubled.

questions.question: The enthalpy change of formation of MgCl(s) is -94 kJ mol^-1 and that of MgCl2(s) is -643 kJ mol^-1. Calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction 2MgCl(s) -> Mg(s) + MgCl2(s). Hence explain why magnesium forms MgCl2 and not MgCl, even though the formation of MgCl is exothermic.
questions.answer: -455 kJ mol^-1; MgCl would change to Mg and MgCl2 exothermically, so MgCl is unstable
steps: Delta H = Delta fH(MgCl2) - 2 x Delta fH(MgCl) = -643 - 2(-94)
Delta H = -455 kJ mol^-1
The reaction is strongly exothermic, so MgCl is unstable with respect to Mg and MgCl2 (it would disproportionate) and is not formed
The large extra energy needed for the second ionisation energy of magnesium (+1451 kJ mol^-1) is more than repaid by the much more exothermic lattice energy of MgCl2 (2+ ion, stronger attraction)
accept: MgCl2 is thermodynamically more stable than MgCl relative to Mg and Cl2: -643 kJ mol^-1 compared with -94 kJ mol^-1
The lattice energy of MgCl2 (-2526 kJ mol^-1) is far more exothermic than that of MgCl (-753 kJ mol^-1) because Mg2+ has a higher charge and charge density than Mg+
Mg+ in MgCl is both oxidised (to Mg2+) and reduced (to Mg), so MgCl disproportionates

questions.question: Which reaction has the most positive entropy change of the system? A CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g), B N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g), C H2O(g) -> H2O(l), D 2Mg(s) + O2(g) -> 2MgO(s).
steps: Entropy increases when a gas is formed from solids because gas particles have many more ways of arranging themselves and their energy.
B decreases the number of moles of gas from 4 to 2, C is condensation, and D uses up a gas to make a solid: all three decrease the entropy of the system.

questions.question: A reaction has Delta H = -126 kJ mol^-1 and a system entropy change of -175 J K^-1 mol^-1 at 298 K. What is the total entropy change? A -598 J K^-1 mol^-1, B -175 J K^-1 mol^-1, C +598 J K^-1 mol^-1, D +248 J K^-1 mol^-1.
steps: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T = +126 000 / 298 = +423 J K^-1 mol^-1 (Delta H converted to J).
Delta S total = Delta S system + Delta S surroundings = -175 + 423 = +248 J K^-1 mol^-1.
A has the wrong sign for Delta S surroundings, B forgets to convert kJ to J, C has the wrong sign for Delta S system.

questions.question: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H2O2(l) -> 2H2O(l) + O2(g). State the sign of the entropy change of the system for this reaction and explain your answer.
questions.answer: Positive, because a gas is formed from liquids
steps: The sign is positive (the entropy of the system increases)
A gas (oxygen) is formed from liquids; gas particles are far more disordered, with many more ways of arranging the particles and distributing energy
accept: The number of moles of gas increases from 0 to 1
Gaseous particles move freely and randomly, unlike particles in a liquid
There are more ways of distributing the energy among the particles in the products

questions.question: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g), Delta H = +178 kJ mol^-1. The standard molar entropies are CaCO3(s) = 92.9, CaO(s) = 39.7 and CO2(g) = 213.6 J K^-1 mol^-1. Calculate the entropy change of the system.
steps: Delta S system = sum of S(products) - sum of S(reactants).

questions.question: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g), Delta H = +178 kJ mol^-1. The entropy change of the system is +160.4 J K^-1 mol^-1. Calculate the total entropy change at 298 K and deduce whether the decomposition is feasible at this temperature.
questions.answer: -437 J K^-1 mol^-1; not feasible at 298 K
steps: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T = -178 000 / 298 = -597.3 J K^-1 mol^-1 (1 mark).
Delta S total is negative, so the decomposition is not feasible at 298 K (1 mark).

questions.question: For the decomposition CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g), Delta H = +178 kJ mol^-1 and the entropy change of the system is +160.4 J K^-1 mol^-1. Calculate the minimum temperature at which the decomposition becomes feasible.
steps: The reaction becomes feasible when Delta S total = 0: Delta S system - Delta H / T = 0 (1 mark).
T = Delta H / Delta S system = 178 000 / 160.4 (1 mark).
T = 1110 K (1109.7 K, which is 837 C) (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain why a reaction with a positive Delta H and a positive entropy change of the system can become feasible if the temperature is increased.
questions.answer: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T is negative but gets smaller in size as T rises, so Delta S total becomes positive
steps: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T is negative for an endothermic reaction, but its size falls as T increases
Delta S system is positive and changes little with T, so above a certain temperature Delta S total = Delta S system + Delta S surroundings becomes positive and the reaction is feasible
accept: At high temperature the entropy increase of the system outweighs the entropy decrease of the surroundings
The minimum temperature is found when Delta S total = 0, that is T = Delta H / Delta S system
Delta S total must be greater than (or equal to) zero for a reaction to be feasible

questions.question: For a reaction at 298 K, the total entropy change is +95.0 J K^-1 mol^-1. Use the relationship Delta S total = R ln K to calculate the value of the equilibrium constant, K, at this temperature. R = 8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1.
steps: Rearrange Delta S total = R ln K to give ln K = Delta S total / R (1 mark).

questions.question: The enthalpy change of solution of ammonium nitrate is +25.7 kJ mol^-1 and the entropy change of the system for dissolving is +108.7 J K^-1 mol^-1. Calculate the total entropy change at 298 K for NH4NO3(s) -> NH4+(aq) + NO3-(aq).
steps: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T = -25 700 / 298 = -86.2 J K^-1 mol^-1 (1 mark).
Delta S total = Delta S system + Delta S surroundings (1 mark).

questions.question: Ammonium nitrate dissolves in water even though the process is endothermic and the temperature of the solution falls. Explain this in terms of entropy changes.
questions.answer: Delta S system is positive and larger in size than the negative Delta S surroundings, so Delta S total is positive
steps: The ordered crystal lattice breaks up into free ions in solution, so the entropy of the system increases (Delta S system is positive)
The process is endothermic: energy is taken from the surroundings, so the entropy of the surroundings decreases (Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T is negative)
Delta S total = Delta S system + Delta S surroundings
The increase in entropy of the system is larger than the decrease in entropy of the surroundings, so Delta S total is positive and dissolving is feasible
accept: The ions in solution are free to move, giving many more ways of arranging the particles and the energy
The size of Delta S surroundings is small because Delta H is small (+25.7 kJ mol^-1)
The reaction is feasible (spontaneous) because Delta S total is greater than zero, even though Delta H is positive
Quoting Delta S total = +22.5 J K^-1 mol^-1, from (a), as evidence

questions.question: The reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g) has a negative Delta H and a negative entropy change of the system. The reaction CH4(g) + H2O(g) -> CO(g) + 3H2(g) has a positive Delta H and a positive entropy change of the system. Discuss how a change in temperature affects the feasibility of each reaction, using Delta S total = Delta S system - Delta H / T.
questions.answer: Ammonia synthesis is feasible at low temperature but not at high temperature; steam reforming is feasible only at high temperature
steps: Ammonia synthesis: Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T is positive, but Delta S system is negative
At low temperature Delta S surroundings is large, so Delta S total is positive and the reaction is feasible
As T increases Delta S surroundings gets smaller, so above T = Delta H / Delta S system, Delta S total is negative and the reaction is not feasible
